💡 Speech Tip: Native speakers link the sounds smoothly. The "d" in "onda" is soft and voiced, with the tongue barely touching the upper teeth.

🔍 Phrase Cultural & Grammar Context

Mexico & Central America

In Mexico and parts of Latin America, "¿Qué onda?" is by far the most popular informal greeting among friends, coworkers of similar age, and young people. In Spain, you will hear "¿Qué pasa?" or "¿Cómo vas?". Dropping the formal "¿Cómo está usted?" avoids creating unnatural social distance.

onda

Noun • Feminine
Literal vs Conversational Meaning:

Literally "wave" (physics/water). In Mexican everyday speech, it translates to "vibe", "groove", or "news".

Pronunciation & Stress:

[OHN-dah] — Stress on first syllable ('on'). The 'd' is softer than in English.

How Natives Use It in Speech:

- Buena onda: "Ella es muy buena onda" (She's very cool/friendly).
- ¿Qué onda?: "What's going on?" / "What's the vibe?"
- Mala onda: "Qué mala onda" (What a bummer / that's not cool).
